brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: 3 bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;half-n) in a tight triangle, each with a top cover, plus caps and joint bolts; 29 parts in total.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base at (0,1), facing the user's side.

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 is a mount spike at the corner shared by cells (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0).
The spike carries the platform-sm accessory. A solid spike can't take a platform, so I used a mount spike.

finish.summary: I built a compact three-cell desk unit with a drawer, plus a mount spike carrying a small platform at the corner where the three bases meet. It has two full bases at (0,0) and (1,0) and a north half base at (0,1). The three cells meet at one corner. The drawer sits on the cut face of the half base, and the top of each base has a cover. I added end caps to every open face and bolted the joints. check_build reports no issues and the collision check is clear. plan_build didn't work: it found no offer for any role, so I placed every part with apply instead. I didn't add any props because the brief doesn't describe what the unit will be used for.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
